features.name: Reproducible upstream fetch

features.name: Browser Time Machine

features.name: Dead Link Recovery

features.name: Receipt Vault
features.description: Save confirmation pages and PDFs of purchases, bookings and government procedures in a searchable vault.

features.name: Already Searched

features.name: Video Search
features.description: Search words inside videos (captions or local speech recognition) and jump to the timestamp.

features.name: Session Guardian
features.description: Warn when a site session is about to expire (where detectable) and protect form progress before logout.

features.name: Login Memory
features.description: Remember which sign-in method was used on each site (password, Google/Apple/GitHub SSO, passkey, email link) without storing secrets.

features.name: Exit Freedom
features.description: Complete export of user data (bookmarks, history, passwords with warning, workspaces, highlights, rules, settings) to open, documented formats.
features.problem: Browsers lock users in by making data hard to take elsewhere.

features.name: Clean Web native content blocking
features.description: Native ad and tracker blocking (candidate engine: adblock-rust) with standard filter lists, cosmetic filtering and per-site toggles.

features.limitations: Filter lists carry their own licenses (some GPL or CC BY-SA) and update channels; blocking always causes some site breakage and sites may use anti-adblock measures.

features.name: Pop-up blocking
features.description: Chromium pop-up blocker plus stricter blocking of pop-unders and click-hijacking new windows.
features.problem: Abusive pop-unders and new-window redirects remain common on low-quality sites.

features.privacy_risk: Low — designed to reduce data exposure.
features.evidence: Competitor precedent: Brave Shields, Firefox ETP, Safari ITP.
features.limitations: Distinguishing legitimate new windows (OAuth, payments) from pop-unders is heuristic; stricter blocking risks breaking login flows.

features.name: Autoplay blocking
features.description: Block audible and optionally all autoplay video by default with per-site exceptions.
features.problem: Autoplaying video wastes data, battery and attention.

features.limitations: Blocking all autoplay breaks some video-first sites and background previews; muted autoplay is allowed by default upstream and changing that has compatibility cost.

features.name: Automated optional-cookie rejection
features.description: Automatically reject optional cookies in consent banners where reliable (CMP APIs, rules), otherwise hide banners conservatively.
features.problem: Consent banners waste time and nudge users into accepting tracking.

features.privacy_risk: Low — designed to reduce data exposure.
features.evidence: Competitor precedent: Brave Shields, Firefox ETP, Safari ITP.
features.limitations: Legal effect of automated rejection varies; reliability differs per CMP.

features.name: Notification prompt blocking
features.description: Quiet or block notification permission prompts by default, with explicit opt-in per site.
features.problem: Notification prompts are spammy and used for scams.
features.use_case: A user is never interrupted by a notification prompt unless they opted to allow prompts for that site.
features.resource_cost: Low — native implementations should reduce page work; must be measured.

features.security_risk: Medium — runs on untrusted web content; parsers must be memory-safe or sandboxed.
features.privacy_risk: Low — designed to reduce data exposure.
features.evidence: Competitor precedent: Brave Shields, Firefox ETP, Safari ITP.
features.limitations: Blocking prompts may hide notifications users actually want (chat, calendar); per-site opt-in must be easy to find.

features.name: Fingerprinting protection
features.description: Reduce fingerprinting surface (farbling/randomization or normalization of high-entropy APIs) while preserving compatibility.
features.problem: Fingerprinting tracks users without cookies.
features.use_case: A tracker script cannot obtain a stable canvas/WebGL/audio fingerprint across sites.
features.resource_cost: Low — native implementations should reduce page work; must be measured.
features.infra_cost: Low — filter list and metadata hosting/mirroring.

features.privacy_risk: Low — designed to reduce data exposure.
features.evidence: Competitor precedent: Brave Shields, Firefox ETP, Safari ITP.
acceptance: Measured with public fingerprinting test suites
features.limitations: Patches in Blink are expensive to maintain; start with low-risk APIs.

features.name: Tracking parameter stripping
features.description: Remove known tracking parameters (utm_*, fbclid, gclid, etc.) from navigations and copied links.
features.problem: Shared links carry tracking identifiers.
features.use_case: A user copies a link and the fbclid parameter is removed.
features.resource_cost: Low — native implementations should reduce page work; must be measured.
features.infra_cost: Low — filter list and metadata hosting/mirroring.
features.security_risk: Medium — runs on untrusted web content; parsers must be memory-safe or sandboxed.
features.privacy_risk: Low — designed to reduce data exposure.
features.evidence: Competitor precedent: Brave Shields, Firefox ETP, Safari ITP.
features.limitations: Parameter lists need maintenance; stripping can break links that misuse tracking-like parameters for function (e.g. affiliate or campaign landing pages).

features.name: Malicious redirect protection
features.description: Block or confirm suspicious redirect chains, bounce tracking and redirect-based malvertising.
features.problem: Redirect chains send users to scams or track them.
features.use_case: Clicking a shortened link that bounces through five trackers lands directly or asks first.
features.resource_cost: Low — native implementations should reduce page work; must be measured.
features.infra_cost: Low — filter list and metadata hosting/mirroring.
features.security_risk: Medium — runs on untrusted web content; parsers must be memory-safe or sandboxed.
features.privacy_risk: Low — designed to reduce data exposure.
features.evidence: Competitor precedent: Brave Shields, Firefox ETP, Safari ITP.
features.limitations: Some legitimate flows (SSO, payment 3-D Secure) are redirect chains; aggressive interstitials would break them, so only known bounce trackers are debounced by default.

features.name: Smart Back
features.description: Protect the Back button from history manipulation (history stuffing, back-button hijacking).
features.problem: Some sites trap users by inserting fake history entries.
features.use_case: Pressing Back on a spammy site actually leaves the site.
features.resource_cost: Low — native implementations should reduce page work; must be measured.
features.infra_cost: Low — filter list and metadata hosting/mirroring.
features.security_risk: Medium — runs on untrusted web content; parsers must be memory-safe or sandboxed.
features.privacy_risk: Low — designed to reduce data exposure.
features.evidence: Chromium has partial history manipulation intervention; Brumel extends it (to be verified).
acceptance: Skips entries created without user activation
features.limitations: Distinguishing manipulative history entries from legitimate single-page-app navigation is heuristic; upstream interventions already exist and must not be duplicated inconsistently.

features.name: Self Repair
features.description: When a page breaks, guided diagnosis that toggles blocking, extensions, fingerprinting protection and identity to find the cause.
features.problem: Privacy features break sites and users do not know which one.
features.use_case: A checkout page fails; Self Repair finds fingerprinting protection caused it and offers a site exception.
features.resource_cost: Low — native implementations should reduce page work; must be measured.
features.infra_cost: Low — filter list and metadata hosting/mirroring.
features.security_risk: Medium — runs on untrusted web content; parsers must be memory-safe or sandboxed.
features.privacy_risk: Low — designed to reduce data exposure.
features.evidence: Competitor precedent: Brave Shields, Firefox ETP, Safari ITP.
features.limitations: Automated bisecting can only test Brumel-side factors (blocking, extensions, protections); site bugs or server issues will still look like breakage.

features.name: Permission Timeline
features.description: History of when each site used camera, microphone, location, clipboard, notifications and other permissions.
features.problem: Users cannot audit which sites actually used sensitive permissions.
features.use_case: A user sees a site accessed location at 3 a.m. and revokes it.
features.resource_cost: Low — native implementations should reduce page work; must be measured.
features.infra_cost: Low — filter list and metadata hosting/mirroring.
features.security_risk: Medium — runs on untrusted web content; parsers must be memory-safe or sandboxed.
features.privacy_risk: Low — designed to reduce data exposure.
features.evidence: Competitor precedent: Brave Shields, Firefox ETP, Safari ITP.
features.limitations: Chromium does not log every permission use (e.g. continuous location watching) at fine granularity; the timeline may show grants and use sessions rather than each access.

features.name: One-Time Permissions
features.description: Grant permissions only for the current visit or a limited time.
features.problem: Permanent grants accumulate for sites used once.
features.use_case: A user allows camera for one video call; it is revoked when the tab closes.
features.resource_cost: Low — native implementations should reduce page work; must be measured.
features.infra_cost: Low — filter list and metadata hosting/mirroring.
features.security_risk: Medium — runs on untrusted web content; parsers must be memory-safe or sandboxed.
features.privacy_risk: Low — designed to reduce data exposure.
features.evidence: Competitor precedent: Brave Shields, Firefox ETP, Safari ITP.
features.limitations: Chromium already supports one-time grants for some permissions; extending to all permission types requires patching permission UI code that changes often upstream.

features.name: Extension Firewall
features.description: Control which sites, network destinations and APIs each extension can access, beyond the standard permission model.
features.problem: Extensions often request access to all sites and can exfiltrate data.
features.use_case: A user restricts an extension to two sites and blocks its access to a tracking endpoint.
features.resource_cost: Low — native implementations should reduce page work; must be measured.
features.infra_cost: Low — filter list and metadata hosting/mirroring.
features.security_risk: Medium — must be enforced in the browser/network service, not in the renderer.
features.privacy_risk: Low — designed to reduce data exposure.
features.evidence: Competitor precedent: Brave Shields, Firefox ETP, Safari ITP.
acceptance: No extension can bypass via the browser process
features.limitations: Extensions with debugger, proxy or native-messaging permissions can bypass site restrictions; Extension Firewall reduces but cannot eliminate extension risk.

features.name: Privacy Receipt
features.description: Per-site and periodic summary of what was blocked, which permissions were used and which connections the browser made.
features.problem: Privacy protection is invisible, so users cannot judge it.
features.use_case: A user sees that a recipe site attempted 37 tracker requests, all blocked.
features.resource_cost: Low — native implementations should reduce page work; must be measured.
features.infra_cost: Low — filter list and metadata hosting/mirroring.
features.security_risk: Medium — runs on untrusted web content; parsers must be memory-safe or sandboxed.
features.privacy_risk: Low — designed to reduce data exposure.
features.evidence: Competitor precedent: Brave Shields, Firefox ETP, Safari ITP.
acceptance: Numbers are actual counts, not estimates
features.limitations: Counts reflect what Brumel blocked or observed; they say nothing about data collected server-side or through first-party tracking that was not blocked.

features.name: Smart Cleanup
features.description: Selective clearing of cookies/storage/cache while keeping chosen logins and sessions.
features.problem: 'Clear browsing data' forces users to choose between privacy and staying logged in.
features.use_case: A user clears all site data except their email and bank sessions.
features.resource_cost: Low — native implementations should reduce page work; must be measured.
features.infra_cost: Low — filter list and metadata hosting/mirroring.
features.security_risk: Medium — runs on untrusted web content; parsers must be memory-safe or sandboxed.
features.privacy_risk: Low — designed to reduce data exposure.
features.evidence: Competitor precedent: Brave Shields, Firefox ETP, Safari ITP.
features.limitations: Keeping some sites' cookies while deleting others can leave cross-site state through first-party partitions; results must be explained, not promised as 'clean'.

features.name: Link Inspector
features.description: Show the real destination, redirect chain and known reputation of a link before opening.
features.problem: Shortened and disguised links hide scams.
features.use_case: A user hovers a shortened link and sees it resolves to a lookalike banking domain.
features.resource_cost: Low — native implementations should reduce page work; must be measured.
features.infra_cost: Low — filter list and metadata hosting/mirroring.
features.security_risk: Medium — runs on untrusted web content; parsers must be memory-safe or sandboxed.
features.privacy_risk: Low — designed to reduce data exposure.
features.evidence: Competitor precedent: Brave Shields, Firefox ETP, Safari ITP.
acceptance: Resolution happens only on user request (avoids pinging trackers)
features.limitations: Resolving redirects requires visiting intermediate URLs, which may itself track the user or trigger actions; resolution is on request only.

features.name: Clipboard Guard
features.description: Notify or block when pages read or overwrite the clipboard, especially crypto addresses and code-paste attacks.
features.problem: Malicious pages hijack the clipboard (e.g. swapping wallet addresses or 'paste this command' scams).
features.use_case: A page tries to replace the copied text with a terminal command and Brumel warns.

features.infra_cost: Low — filter list and metadata hosting/mirroring.
features.security_risk: Low — mitigation.
features.privacy_risk: Low — designed to reduce data exposure.
features.evidence: Competitor precedent: Brave Shields, Firefox ETP, Safari ITP.
acceptance: Clipboard writes without user gesture blocked or flagged
features.limitations: Detecting malicious clipboard writes is heuristic; legitimate 'copy' buttons write without explicit selection and must keep working.

features.name: Settings Lock
features.description: Tracked together with ENG-016 (Update Guard).
features.problem: Browser updates sometimes reset settings or re-enable features users turned off.
features.use_case: Preserve user preferences after updates and against extension changes.
features.resource_cost: Low — sampling and policy evaluation in the browser process; must be measured.
features.security_risk: Low — must not weaken process isolation.
features.privacy_risk: Low — resource data stays local.
features.evidence: Hypothesis: resource savings must be proven with the public benchmark suite.

Use case verified: Preserve user preferences after updates and against extension changes.
features.limitations: Technical duplicate merged into ENG-016; kept as its own entry to preserve the use case and traceability.

features.name: Biometric lock
features.description: Lock the browser, private spaces or password reveal behind OS authentication (Windows Hello, polkit/PAM).
features.problem: Shared or unattended computers expose browser data.
features.use_case: A user requires Windows Hello to reveal saved passwords and open the Finance space.
features.resource_cost: Low — native implementations should reduce page work; must be measured.

acceptance: No biometric data handled by Brumel
features.limitations: Windows Hello and PAM/polkit offer different guarantees; on Linux biometric support depends on distribution setup and may be unavailable.

features.name: Local data encryption
features.description: Encrypt sensitive Brumel Store data at rest using OS-protected keys (OSCrypt) and optional user passphrase.
features.problem: Profile files can be copied by malware or other users.
features.use_case: Copying a profile folder to another machine does not reveal archived tabs or drafts.

features.evidence: Competitor precedent: Brave Shields, Firefox ETP, Safari ITP.
acceptance: Key handling documented in threat model
features.limitations: Encryption at rest cannot protect against malware running as the same user.

features.name: End-to-end encrypted sync
features.description: Tracked together with CON-020 (Client-side E2EE layer).
features.problem: Server breaches or operators should never expose synced data.
features.use_case: Sync protected so the server cannot read user data.
features.resource_cost: Low — incremental sync, batched network activity.
features.infra_cost: Medium — relay/storage costs grow with users; self-hosting must be possible.

features.evidence: Competitor precedent: Firefox Sync and Brave Sync (E2EE designs).

Use case verified: Sync protected so the server cannot read user data.
features.limitations: Technical duplicate merged into CON-020; kept as its own entry to preserve the use case and traceability.

features.name: Credential protection
features.description: Harden the password store: reauthentication for reveal/export, breach checks via privacy-preserving k-anonymity, phishing-resistant autofill.

features.problem: Self-hosters want to use their own larger models.
features.use_case: A user points Brumel at an Ollama server on their LAN.
features.resource_cost: High while loaded (hundreds of MB RAM, CPU/GPU/NPU bursts); zero when unloaded.
features.security_risk: High — web content is untrusted input to the model (prompt injection).
features.privacy_risk: Medium — local only by default; data never leaves the device without explicit opt-in.
features.evidence: Research: quality of sub-1B models for each task is unproven and must be benchmarked.
features.limitations: Local-network endpoints expose Brumel to a new class of targets (LAN services); TLS and authentication of self-hosted endpoints vary widely.

features.name: API key storage
features.description: Secure storage and rotation of BYOK keys using OS-protected encryption.
features.problem: API keys in plain config files get stolen.
features.use_case: A user stores a key once and can revoke it from settings.
features.resource_cost: High while loaded (hundreds of MB RAM, CPU/GPU/NPU bursts); zero when unloaded.
features.security_risk: High — web content is untrusted input to the model (prompt injection).
features.privacy_risk: Medium — local only by default; data never leaves the device without explicit opt-in.
features.evidence: Research: quality of sub-1B models for each task is unproven and must be benchmarked.
acceptance: Never exposed to web content or extensions
features.limitations: OS-protected storage does not protect keys from malware running as the user; keys must be scoped and revocable at the provider.

features.name: Small-model security decisions
features.description: Proposal pattern: use a small local model to decide phishing, malware, permissions or other security outcomes.
features.problem: Small models are unreliable and manipulable by content.
features.use_case: N/A — rejected. Alternative: deterministic protections (CORE-050, SHD-016, SHD-036).
features.resource_cost: High while loaded (hundreds of MB RAM, CPU/GPU/NPU bursts); zero when unloaded.
features.security_risk: Critical — prompt injection and false negatives.
features.privacy_risk: Medium — local only by default; data never leaves the device without explicit opt-in.
features.evidence: Research: quality of sub-1B models for each task is unproven and must be benchmarked.
acceptance: No security decision depends solely on model output
features.limitations: Rejected by project principle (section E).

features.name: Autonomous agents on small models
features.description: Proposal pattern: let a small local model act autonomously (click, submit, purchase) in the browser.
features.problem: Autonomous browser agents are highly exposed to prompt injection and errors.
features.use_case: N/A — rejected as stated. Alternative: SHD-037 Agent Clean Room research before any agent.
features.resource_cost: High while loaded (hundreds of MB RAM, CPU/GPU/NPU bursts); zero when unloaded.
features.security_risk: Critical.
features.privacy_risk: Medium — local only by default; data never leaves the device without explicit opt-in.
features.evidence: Research: quality of sub-1B models for each task is unproven and must be benchmarked.
acceptance: No autonomous agent ships without SHD-037
features.limitations: Rejected as stated; see SHD-037.

features.name: Unverified AI factual comparisons
features.description: Proposal pattern: small-model comparisons of products or facts without source verification.
features.problem: Hallucinated comparisons mislead purchasing and decisions.
features.use_case: N/A — rejected. Alternative: WRK-029 Smart Compare with verifiable extraction.
features.resource_cost: High while loaded (hundreds of MB RAM, CPU/GPU/NPU bursts); zero when unloaded.
features.security_risk: High — web content is untrusted input to the model (prompt injection).
features.privacy_risk: Medium — local only by default; data never leaves the device without explicit opt-in.
features.evidence: Research: quality of sub-1B models for each task is unproven and must be benchmarked.
acceptance: No comparison value is shown without a source anchor
features.limitations: Rejected as stated; see WRK-029.

features.name: Smart Continuity
features.description: Optional, end-to-end encrypted multi-device sync of Brumel data with local-first operation.
features.problem: Users want continuity without giving a company readable access to their data.
features.use_case: A user opens their laptop and finds the workspaces they organized on their desktop.
features.resource_cost: Low — incremental sync, batched network activity.
features.infra_cost: Medium — relay/storage costs grow with users; self-hosting must be possible.
features.security_risk: High — key management and server compromise must not expose data.
features.privacy_risk: Medium — metadata (timing, sizes, device count) visible to relay even with E2EE.
features.evidence: Competitor precedent: Firefox Sync and Brave Sync (E2EE designs).
acceptance: Browser fully functional without sync or account
features.limitations: E2EE prevents server-side features (web access to data, server-side search, account recovery without key); losing all devices and the recovery key loses data.

features.name: Device Mesh
features.description: Direct device-to-device sync over WebRTC/LAN when devices can reach each other, relay as fallback.
features.problem: Routing all sync through a server adds cost and metadata exposure.
features.use_case: Two devices on the same network sync directly without the relay.
features.resource_cost: Low — incremental sync, batched network activity.
features.infra_cost: Medium — relay/storage costs grow with users; self-hosting must be possible.

features.evidence: Competitor precedent: Firefox Sync and Brave Sync (E2EE designs).
features.limitations: Direct connections fail behind symmetric NAT and corporate networks; local discovery (mDNS) can be blocked or raise privacy concerns.

features.name: Quick Share

features.evidence: Competitor precedent: Firefox Sync and Brave Sync (E2EE designs).
features.limitations: File size is limited by relay capacity and cost; both devices may need to be online at the same time for mesh transfers.

features.name: Send tab to device

features.name: Bookmark sync

features.name: Workspace sync
features.description: E2EE sync of workspaces, folders and tab lists.
features.problem: Workspace organization is lost when switching devices.

acceptance: Unloaded tabs sync as metadata only
features.limitations: Workspace data references tabs and identities that may not exist on the other device; heavy workspaces mean larger sync payloads.

features.name: Preferences sync
features.description: E2EE sync of selected settings with device-specific exclusions.
features.problem: Reconfiguring each device is tedious.
features.use_case: A user's Shield settings apply on all devices.

features.evidence: Competitor precedent: Firefox Sync and Brave Sync (E2EE designs).

features.name: Rules sync
features.description: E2EE sync of routing, profile and download rules.

features.use_case: Smart Router rules apply on both computers.

features.infra_cost: Medium — relay/storage costs grow with users; self-hosting must be possible.

features.evidence: Competitor precedent: Firefox Sync and Brave Sync (E2EE designs).
features.limitations: Rules may reference device-specific paths or identities; conflicting rule edits need manual resolution.

features.name: Optional history sync
features.description: Opt-in E2EE history sync with retention limits.
features.problem: History search fails on another device.
features.use_case: A user finds on laptop a page visited on desktop.
features.resource_cost: Low — incremental sync, batched network activity.
features.infra_cost: Medium — relay/storage costs grow with users; self-hosting must be possible.
features.security_risk: High — key management and server compromise must not expose data.
features.privacy_risk: High — history is sensitive; opt-in.
features.evidence: Competitor precedent: Firefox Sync and Brave Sync (E2EE designs).
features.limitations: History is high-volume and highly sensitive; syncing it increases metadata exposure (sizes, timing) even with E2EE.

features.name: Optional extension sync
features.description: Sync the list of installed compatible extensions (not their data).
features.problem: Reinstalling extensions per device is tedious.
features.use_case: A new device offers to install the same extensions.
features.resource_cost: Low — incremental sync, batched network activity.
features.infra_cost: Medium — relay/storage costs grow with users; self-hosting must be possible.
features.security_risk: High — key management and server compromise must not expose data.

features.evidence: Competitor precedent: Firefox Sync and Brave Sync (E2EE designs).
features.limitations: Extension data and settings are not synced, so extensions need reconfiguration; extension availability can differ by platform.

features.name: Clipboard sync
features.description: Explicit, authorized clipboard sharing between paired devices.
features.problem: Copying between devices requires workarounds.
features.use_case: A user copies a code on phone and pastes it on desktop.
features.resource_cost: Low — incremental sync, batched network activity.
features.infra_cost: Medium — relay/storage costs grow with users; self-hosting must be possible.

acceptance: Explicit per-use action or time-limited authorization
features.limitations: Clipboards frequently contain passwords and codes; even authorized sync risks leaking secrets to a compromised paired device.

features.name: Reading continuity
features.description: Sync reading position for queued articles.
features.problem: Users lose their place across devices.
features.use_case: A user continues an article at the same paragraph on another device.
features.resource_cost: Low — incremental sync, batched network activity.
features.infra_cost: Medium — relay/storage costs grow with users; self-hosting must be possible.
features.security_risk: High — key management and server compromise must not expose data.

features.evidence: Competitor precedent: Firefox Sync and Brave Sync (E2EE designs).
acceptance: Position sync for Reading Queue items
features.limitations: Reading positions depend on identical page layout; different screen sizes and dynamic pages make positions approximate.

features.name: QR pairing
features.description: Pair devices by scanning a QR code that carries a one-time key exchange.
features.problem: Typing sync codes is error-prone; account-based pairing requires trusting a server.
features.use_case: A user pairs a laptop by scanning a QR from the desktop.

features.infra_cost: Medium — relay/storage costs grow with users; self-hosting must be possible.

features.evidence: Competitor precedent: Firefox Sync and Brave Sync (E2EE designs).

features.name: Incremental sync
features.description: Operation/delta-based sync instead of full snapshots.
features.problem: Full syncs waste bandwidth and battery.
features.use_case: Changing one bookmark sends a small encrypted operation.
features.resource_cost: Low — incremental sync, batched network activity.
features.infra_cost: Medium — relay/storage costs grow with users; self-hosting must be possible.
features.security_risk: High — key management and server compromise must not expose data.
features.privacy_risk: Medium — metadata (timing, sizes, device count) visible to relay even with E2EE.
features.evidence: Competitor precedent: Firefox Sync and Brave Sync (E2EE designs).
features.limitations: Operation logs grow and need compaction; schema changes across Brumel versions must stay backward compatible.

features.name: Conflict management
features.description: Deterministic merge (CRDT or operation log) with visible conflict resolution where needed.
features.problem: Naive last-write-wins loses data.
features.use_case: Two devices edit the same workspace offline and both changes survive.
features.resource_cost: Low — incremental sync, batched network activity.
features.infra_cost: Medium — relay/storage costs grow with users; self-hosting must be possible.
features.security_risk: High — key management and server compromise must not expose data.
features.privacy_risk: Medium — metadata (timing, sizes, device count) visible to relay even with E2EE.
features.evidence: Competitor precedent: Firefox Sync and Brave Sync (E2EE designs).
acceptance: Merge rules documented per data type
features.limitations: Some conflicts have no correct automatic answer (concurrent renames); CRDTs add storage overhead and complexity.

features.name: Offline operation
features.description: All synced features work offline; sync is eventual.
features.problem: Cloud-first sync breaks without connectivity.
features.use_case: A user organizes tabs on a plane; changes sync on landing.
features.resource_cost: Low — incremental sync, batched network activity.
features.infra_cost: Medium — relay/storage costs grow with users; self-hosting must be possible.
features.security_risk: High — key management and server compromise must not expose data.
features.privacy_risk: Medium — metadata (timing, sizes, device count) visible to relay even with E2EE.
features.evidence: Competitor precedent: Firefox Sync and Brave Sync (E2EE designs).
acceptance: No feature requires connectivity to work locally
features.limitations: Long offline periods increase conflict likelihood and payload sizes on reconnect.

features.name: Encrypted backups (remote)
features.description: Optional E2EE backup snapshots stored on the relay or a user-chosen storage.
features.problem: Device loss without backup loses everything.
features.use_case: A user restores to a new device using their recovery key.
features.resource_cost: Low — incremental sync, batched network activity.
features.infra_cost: Medium — relay/storage costs grow with users; self-hosting must be possible.
features.security_risk: High — key management and server compromise must not expose data.

features.evidence: Competitor precedent: Firefox Sync and Brave Sync (E2EE designs).

features.name: Self-hosting
features.description: Official self-hostable sync server (Docker) and documented protocol.
features.problem: Users should not depend on the project's servers.
features.use_case: A self-hoster runs the sync server on their own machine.
features.resource_cost: Low — incremental sync, batched network activity.
features.security_risk: High — key management and server compromise must not expose data.

features.name: Password sync
features.description: Sync of saved passwords and passkeys metadata, only after a dedicated security review.
features.problem: Users expect passwords on all devices, but a flawed design would expose the most sensitive data.
features.use_case: A user's new laptop has their passwords after pairing.
features.resource_cost: Low — incremental sync, batched network activity.
features.infra_cost: Medium — relay/storage costs grow with users; self-hosting must be possible.
features.security_risk: Critical.
features.privacy_risk: Medium — metadata (timing, sizes, device count) visible to relay even with E2EE.
features.evidence: Competitor precedent: Firefox Sync and Brave Sync (E2EE designs).
features.limitations: Deferred until a dedicated review; users can use dedicated password managers meanwhile.

features.name: Client-side E2EE layer
features.description: Key hierarchy, encryption and authentication performed in clients; servers only store opaque ciphertext and minimal metadata.
features.problem: Server breaches or operators should never expose synced data.
features.use_case: Even with full database access, a relay operator cannot read bookmarks.
features.resource_cost: Low — incremental sync, batched network activity.
features.infra_cost: Medium — relay/storage costs grow with users; self-hosting must be possible.
features.security_risk: Critical.
features.privacy_risk: Medium — metadata (timing, sizes, device count) visible to relay even with E2EE.
features.evidence: Competitor precedent: Firefox Sync and Brave Sync (E2EE designs).
acceptance: Threat model and external review before beta
features.limitations: Cryptographic design errors are easy to make; external review is required before beta, and E2EE does not hide metadata such as timing and payload size.

features.security_risk: High — key management and server compromise must not expose data.

features.evidence: Competitor precedent: Firefox Sync and Brave Sync (E2EE designs).

features.name: WebRTC transport
features.description: WebRTC data channels for device mesh with STUN/TURN considerations.
features.problem: P2P needs NAT traversal.
features.use_case: Two devices connect directly through NAT.
features.resource_cost: Low — incremental sync, batched network activity.
features.security_risk: High — key management and server compromise must not expose data.
features.privacy_risk: Medium — metadata (timing, sizes, device count) visible to relay even with E2EE.
features.evidence: Competitor precedent: Firefox Sync and Brave Sync (E2EE designs).
acceptance: Data still E2EE at application level
features.limitations: TURN relays are needed for many networks and cost bandwidth; WebRTC adds a large, security-sensitive dependency already present in Chromium.

features.description: Minimal server API storing and forwarding encrypted blobs and ops.

features.use_case: The relay stores only ciphertext with sizes and timestamps.

features.use_case: Run the sync server with Docker on personal infrastructure.

features.name: Mobile Upload

features.name: Pocket Profile

features.name: Trusted Remote Help

features.problem: Default shortcuts conflict with apps or habits.
features.use_case: A user remaps workspace switching to Alt+1..9.
features.resource_cost: Low — must respect GPU/battery budgets (animations, transparency).
features.security_risk: Low
features.privacy_risk: Low
features.evidence: Competitor precedent; visual preferences validated through community feedback.
features.limitations: Some shortcuts are reserved by the OS or by Chromium security UI (e.g. Guaranteed Exit) and cannot be remapped.

features.name: Command palette
features.description: Tracked together with WRK-018 (Quick Actions).
features.problem: Power features are hidden in menus.
features.use_case: Search-driven command palette for all actions.
features.resource_cost: Low — UI and metadata only; unloaded tabs cost no renderer memory.
features.security_risk: Low
features.privacy_risk: Low — organization metadata stored locally.
features.evidence: Competitor precedent: popular in Arc, Vivaldi and Zen; demand to be validated with users.
acceptance: Covered by the acceptance criteria of WRK-018
Use case verified: Search-driven command palette for all actions.
features.limitations: Technical duplicate merged into WRK-018; kept as its own entry to preserve the use case and traceability.

features.name: Touch support
features.description: Touch-friendly targets and gestures on touchscreen laptops/tablets.
features.problem: Small touch targets on convertibles.
features.use_case: A user on a 2-in-1 navigates tabs by touch.
features.resource_cost: Low — must respect GPU/battery budgets (animations, transparency).
features.security_risk: Low
features.privacy_risk: Low
features.evidence: Competitor precedent; visual preferences validated through community feedback.
features.limitations: Chromium's touch UI on Windows/Linux is less mature than mobile; gestures may conflict with OS-level touch gestures.

features.name: Familiar default layout
features.description: Default layout close to mainstream browsers so new users feel at home; advanced layouts are opt-in.
features.problem: Radical defaults scare switchers.
features.use_case: A Chrome user starts Brumel and immediately knows where everything is.
features.resource_cost: Low — must respect GPU/battery budgets (animations, transparency).
features.security_risk: Low
features.privacy_risk: Low
features.evidence: Competitor precedent; visual preferences validated through community feedback.
acceptance: Advanced features off or subtle by default
features.limitations: A familiar default hides Brumel's differentiators at first; discoverability depends on Progressive disclosure working well.

features.name: Progressive disclosure
features.description: Advanced features revealed gradually based on use and explicit choice, not all at once.
features.problem: Hundreds of features overwhelm users.
features.use_case: After a user keeps 30+ tabs for a week, Brumel suggests vertical tabs once.
features.resource_cost: Low — must respect GPU/battery budgets (animations, transparency).
features.security_risk: Low
features.privacy_risk: Low
features.evidence: Competitor precedent; visual preferences validated through community feedback.
acceptance: Local logic only, no telemetry required
The default-browser question is asked at most once, at first run, and never repeated
features.limitations: Usage-based suggestions require local usage tracking; poorly timed suggestions feel like nagging, so frequency must be strictly limited.

features.name: Progressive Discovery
features.description: Tracked together with UI-019 (Progressive disclosure).
features.problem: Hundreds of features overwhelm users.
features.use_case: Discover new features according to the user's needs.
features.resource_cost: Low — must respect GPU/battery budgets (animations, transparency).
features.security_risk: Low
features.privacy_risk: Low
features.evidence: Competitor precedent; visual preferences validated through community feedback.
acceptance: Covered by the acceptance criteria of UI-019
Use case verified: Discover new features according to the user's needs.
features.limitations: Technical duplicate merged into UI-019; kept as its own entry to preserve the use case and traceability.

features.name: Configuration Recipes
features.description: Share configurations (profiles, rules, layout) as files without personal data.
features.problem: Good setups cannot be shared easily.
features.use_case: A user imports a 'Low-end laptop' recipe from the community.
features.resource_cost: Low — must respect GPU/battery budgets (animations, transparency).
features.security_risk: Low
features.privacy_risk: Low
features.evidence: Competitor precedent; visual preferences validated through community feedback.
features.limitations: Validating that a recipe contains no personal data is hard (URLs, names in rules); applying third-party recipes can weaken privacy settings.

features.name: Quiet New Tab page
features.description: A calm New Tab page with a search box, the user's own shortcuts and an optional resume strip, with no feed, no sponsored tiles and no remote content by default.
features.problem: Mainstream New Tab pages carry news feeds, sponsored tiles and remote content that add noise and network requests.
features.use_case: A user opens a new tab and sees only the search box and the sites they pinned; nothing loads from the network until they type.
features.resource_cost: Low — must respect GPU/battery budgets (animations, transparency).
features.security_risk: Low
features.privacy_risk: Low
features.evidence: Competitor precedent: Firefox and Brave let users turn off New Tab content; Edge and Chrome ship feeds by default.
acceptance: No network request is made by the New Tab page itself until the user acts
No sponsored or remote content, on by default or otherwise
Every element can be hidden, including the shortcuts
Meets the design-system accessibility baseline in light, dark and forced-colours modes
features.limitations: Upstream Chromium's New Tab page is tied to Google services; Brumel replaces it with its own WebUI page, which is a larger patch than restyling.

features.name: REST API client
features.description: Built-in HTTP request builder.
features.problem: Developers switch to separate tools for quick API calls.
features.use_case: A developer tests an endpoint with auth headers.
features.resource_cost: Low — loaded only when enabled.
features.security_risk: High — developer and automation features expand the privileged surface.
features.privacy_risk: Low
features.evidence: Research: demand from developers to be validated; many needs are already met by DevTools.
features.limitations: Overlaps with mature tools (DevTools, curl, dedicated clients); maintaining parity with their features is not a goal.

features.name: WebSocket client
features.description: Connect, send and inspect WebSocket messages.
features.problem: Debugging sockets needs external tools.
features.use_case: A developer sends test frames.
features.resource_cost: Low — loaded only when enabled.
features.security_risk: High — developer and automation features expand the privileged surface.
features.privacy_risk: Low
features.evidence: Research: demand from developers to be validated; many needs are already met by DevTools.
features.limitations: Limited to WebSocket; other protocols (gRPC, MQTT) are out of scope.

features.name: JSON viewer and editor
features.description: Pretty JSON viewing with folding, search and editing.
features.problem: Raw JSON is unreadable.
features.use_case: A developer browses a large API response.
features.resource_cost: Low — loaded only when enabled.
features.security_risk: High — developer and automation features expand the privileged surface.
features.privacy_risk: Low
features.evidence: Research: demand from developers to be validated; many needs are already met by DevTools.
features.limitations: Very large JSON (hundreds of MB) may exceed renderer memory; Chromium's built-in JSON viewer was removed/limited upstream, so this is Brumel-owned code to maintain.

features.name: Storage viewer
features.description: User-friendly view of site storage beyond DevTools.
features.problem: DevTools storage panels are scattered.
features.use_case: A developer inspects IndexedDB of a PWA.
features.resource_cost: Low — loaded only when enabled.
features.security_risk: High — developer and automation features expand the privileged surface.
features.privacy_risk: Low
features.evidence: Research: demand from developers to be validated; many needs are already met by DevTools.
features.limitations: DevTools already exposes storage; a separate viewer duplicates functionality and must keep up with storage API changes.

features.name: Network diagnostics
features.description: DNS, TLS and connectivity diagnostics page.
features.problem: Diagnosing connection issues requires several tools.
features.use_case: A user checks why a site fails TLS.
features.resource_cost: Low — loaded only when enabled.
features.security_risk: High — developer and automation features expand the privileged surface.
features.privacy_risk: Low
features.evidence: Research: demand from developers to be validated; many needs are already met by DevTools.
features.limitations: Diagnostics run inside the browser's network stack and cannot replace OS tools (traceroute, packet capture) without privileged access, which is out of scope.

features.name: Per-workspace proxies
features.description: Assign a proxy configuration per workspace or identity.
features.problem: Chromium proxy settings are global.
features.use_case: A developer routes the 'Staging' workspace through a proxy.
features.resource_cost: Low — loaded only when enabled.
features.security_risk: Medium — misrouting risks leaks.
features.privacy_risk: Low
features.evidence: Research: demand from developers to be validated; many needs are already met by DevTools.
features.limitations: Requires network-context changes; complexity high.

features.name: Mobile emulation
features.description: Tracked together with CORE-035 (DevTools).
features.problem: Developers need standard tooling.
features.use_case: Emulate mobile devices (DevTools device mode).
features.resource_cost: Inherited from Chromium; no Brumel-specific overhead expected.
features.security_risk: Medium — must track upstream security fixes without regressions.
features.privacy_risk: Low — Google service endpoints must be removed or replaced.
features.evidence: Competitor precedent: standard in Chromium-based browsers.
acceptance: Covered by the acceptance criteria of CORE-035
Use case verified: Emulate mobile devices (DevTools device mode).
features.limitations: Technical duplicate merged into CORE-035; kept as its own entry to preserve the use case and traceability.

features.name: Development auto-reload
features.description: Auto-reload local pages on file change.
features.problem: Manual reloads slow iteration.
features.use_case: A developer's localhost page reloads on save.
features.resource_cost: Low — loaded only when enabled.
features.security_risk: High — developer and automation features expand the privileged surface.
features.privacy_risk: Low
features.evidence: Research: demand from developers to be validated; many needs are already met by DevTools.
features.limitations: Watching local files requires file system access outside the sandbox; scope is limited to localhost-served pages reloading on server signals.

features.resource_cost: Inherited from Chromium; no Brumel-specific overhead expected.

features.evidence: Competitor precedent: standard in Chromium-based browsers.
acceptance: Covered by the acceptance criteria of CORE-035
Use case verified: Lighthouse-style audits (available in DevTools).
features.limitations: Technical duplicate merged into CORE-035; kept as its own entry to preserve the use case and traceability.

features.name: Custom scripts (userscripts)
features.description: Run user-provided scripts on pages.
features.problem: Power users rely on userscript managers.
features.use_case: A user runs a script that adds a button to a site.
features.resource_cost: Low — loaded only when enabled.
features.security_risk: High — script injection risk.
features.privacy_risk: Low
features.evidence: Research: demand from developers to be validated; many needs are already met by DevTools.
features.limitations: Extensions already cover this; Deferred.

features.name: GitHub integration
features.description: Notifications/PR views for GitHub as an optional module.
features.problem: Developers live in GitHub tabs.
features.use_case: A developer sees PR review requests in a panel.
features.resource_cost: Low — loaded only when enabled.
features.security_risk: High — developer and automation features expand the privileged surface.
features.privacy_risk: Low
features.evidence: Research: demand from developers to be validated; many needs are already met by DevTools.
features.limitations: GitHub APIs and rate limits change; a niche integration may not justify maintenance compared with the web UI.

features.name: Playwright automation
features.description: First-class automation hooks for Playwright/CDP.
features.problem: Testing tools need a controllable browser.
features.use_case: A developer runs tests against Brumel.
features.resource_cost: Low — loaded only when enabled.
features.security_risk: High — CDP grants full control.
features.privacy_risk: Low
features.evidence: Research: demand from developers to be validated; many needs are already met by DevTools.
features.limitations: Chromium's remote debugging already allows this; deeper integration Deferred until capability model.

features.name: MCP integration
features.description: Model Context Protocol server/client capabilities for the browser.
features.problem: AI tools want structured browser access.
features.use_case: A local AI tool reads the open tab list with permission.
features.resource_cost: Low — loaded only when enabled.
features.security_risk: High — exposes browser data to external agents.
features.privacy_risk: Low
features.evidence: Research: demand from developers to be validated; many needs are already met by DevTools.
features.limitations: MCP is an evolving protocol; any integration exposes browser data to external agents and is blocked until SHD-037 exists.

features.name: Homelab Mode
features.description: Workspace preset for self-hosted dashboards with local certificates and LAN-friendly settings.
features.problem: Self-hosters fight certificate and LAN warnings.
features.use_case: A self-hoster opens internal dashboards without repeated warnings.
features.resource_cost: Low — loaded only when enabled.
features.security_risk: High — developer and automation features expand the privileged surface.
features.privacy_risk: Low
features.evidence: Research: demand from developers to be validated; many needs are already met by DevTools.
acceptance: Never weakens TLS for public sites
features.limitations: Relaxing warnings for LAN hosts must never weaken TLS validation for public sites; misconfigured scopes could enable interception.

features.name: Self-hosted service management
features.description: Overview of self-hosted services (status, links).
features.problem: Self-hosters juggle many dashboards.
features.use_case: A user sees which home services are down.
features.resource_cost: Low — loaded only when enabled.
features.security_risk: High — developer and automation features expand the privileged surface.
features.privacy_risk: Low
features.evidence: Research: demand from developers to be validated; many needs are already met by DevTools.
features.limitations: Status checks to LAN services reveal network topology and could be abused by web pages if exposed; read-only and browser-UI-only by design.

features.name: Local certificates
features.description: Manage trust of local development CAs per profile.
features.problem: Local HTTPS setups are painful.
features.use_case: A developer trusts a local CA only in the Dev workspace.
features.resource_cost: Low — loaded only when enabled.
features.security_risk: High — custom CAs enable interception.
features.privacy_risk: Low
features.evidence: Research: demand from developers to be validated; many needs are already met by DevTools.
features.limitations: Custom CAs enable traffic interception if misused or stolen; scoping trust per profile requires changes to certificate verification code.

features.name: Local terminal
features.description: Embedded terminal.
features.problem: Developers switch windows to a terminal.
features.use_case: A developer runs a command next to their tab.
features.resource_cost: Low — loaded only when enabled.
features.security_risk: Critical — command execution from the browser.
features.privacy_risk: Low
features.evidence: Research: demand from developers to be validated; many needs are already met by DevTools.
acceptance: Only after SHD-037 and a dedicated threat model
features.limitations: Deferred; OS terminals already exist.
